articles.title: Israeli Settlers Intensify Violence Against Palestinians During Olive Harvest
articles.summary: The olive harvest season in the West Bank has become the most violent on record due to increased attacks by Israeli settlers on Palestinian farmers.
articles.content: Israeli settlers have intensified their attacks on Palestinians during this year's olive harvest in the West Bank, making it the most violent on record according to the United Nations. The annual olive harvest is a significant event for Palestinians, as it allows them to cultivate and sell olives and olive oil, providing sustenance for many families. However, this year's harvest has been marked by increased violence from Israeli settlers, who have disrupted the peaceful tradition of Palestinian farmers. Retired Israeli brigadier general Yoni Shimshoni is part of a group that provides protection to Palestinians during the olive harvest. He and his fellow commanders, all former Israeli generals, have dedicated themselves to defending Palestinians against settler attacks, despite having spent their careers serving as defenders of Israel. Shimshoni notes that Palestinian farmers are now too afraid to tend to their own groves due to the threat of settler violence. The presence of Shimshoni and his team has become a necessary measure to ensure the safety of Palestinian farmers during this critical period. The actions of Shimshoni and his group raise questions about the current state of Israel's internal dynamics, with some viewing their efforts as a sign of a battle within the country over its future. The Palestinian town of Duma is surrounded by three Israeli settlements, where tensions between settlers and locals have been escalating for some time. Israeli settlers have a long history of coveting this land and attempting to push Palestinians out, but recent incidents suggest a new level of brazenness on their part. A group of left-wing activists and former Israeli commanders has been intervening to protect Palestinian farmers during the olive harvest season. Their presence seems to be met with a mixture of hostility and intimidation from the settlers. The atmosphere is tense, with both sides constantly filming each other's actions. This can lead to confrontations, as in the case where a teenage settler tried to wrestle a bag of olives away from a Palestinian woman. Settlers' aggressive behavior towards Palestinians and Westerners, including journalists, has become increasingly common since the October 7 terrorist attacks, which marked the deadliest day in Israeli history. As the olive harvest season gets underway, Israeli settlers have been increasingly aggressive towards Palestinians and Westerners, including journalists. The situation has become so volatile that it's now common to see settlers clashing with both Israelis who are trying to protect the Palestinians and the Palestinian farmers themselves. In Duma, a village in the West Bank, the army has taken on a role that's more akin to an occupying authority than a neutral force. When soldiers arrive, they block all exits, preventing anyone from leaving, including settlers who might be involved in confrontations with Palestinians. The police are then called in, and it's their job to determine which settlers were most provocative. The Israeli commanders who are trying to protect the Palestinian farmers have been detained by the very authorities they're supposed to be working with. Retired Brigadier General Joel Feldschuh, a former fighter pilot and intelligence chief, was among those arrested for trying to help a Palestinian olive picker. When asked why the army was taking this action, he expressed his indignation. The commanders driving between villages in the West Bank are also speaking out against the situation. Major General Eyal Ben-Rueven, who previously commanded the division in that area, said that when he was in charge, the police were sent to work with civilians. He emphasized that the military should be fighting against external threats like Hezbollah and Hamas, not against Jewish settlers. The commanders' actions have sparked a debate about the role of the Israeli army and whether it's being used as a tool by the state to control the population. They're calling for change and want to help shift the country's direction away from violence towards its Palestinian neighbors. The Israeli government's stance on the annexation of the West Bank has been met with criticism from some quarters. Critics argue that the larger settler movement, which has allies within the government, is pushing for a complete takeover of the territory. In a recent conversation, Ophir Falk, Prime Minister Netanyahu's foreign policy adviser, dismissed these allegations. He stated that Israel's government has taken extraordinary measures to address the issue of settler violence in the West Bank, which he and many Israelis refer to as Judea and Samaria. According to Falk, the crime rate in this region is lower than in major cities such as Los Angeles, New York, and London. However, Palestinians living in the area face a different reality. They are subjected to daily attacks from Palestinian terrorists, with over 1,530 attempts at violence recorded in the past year alone. The Israeli government's stance on settler violence has been called into question by some of its own officials. Critics argue that Netanyahu's allies in the government have failed to adequately address the issue, and instead continue to support the settler movement. Meir Goldmintz, an Israeli settler who lives in Shavei Shomron, a settlement outside Nablus in the northern West Bank, has his own perspective on the matter. Born in Jerusalem, he moved to the area 25 years ago and now teaches biblical history to local students. Goldmintz firmly believes that the land of Israel belongs exclusively to the Jewish people. He cites the Old Testament as proof of this claim, pointing out that Shavei Shomron is mentioned specifically in the ancient text. Meir Goldmintz, a settler leader, points out that the biblical narrative supports the Jewish claim to the land. He cites the Old Testament as proof of this claim, referencing the covenant made between God and Abraham, which promises the land from the River of Egypt to the River Prat to their offspring. According to Goldmintz, the Palestinian cities and villages surrounding Shavei Shomron have no inherent connection to the land, much like a victim of theft has no relationship with the thief. He emphasizes that the land was not originally theirs but was taken from its rightful owners while they were in exile. The biblical narrative is on display throughout the region, including the ruins of an ancient temple built after King Solomon's reign. Goldmintz uses these historical sites to support his argument that Jews have a long-standing connection to the land and were forcibly removed by others. articles.title: Ben Shapiro Discusses Republican Party's Future with Amna Nawaz on "Settle In
articles.summary: Ben Shapiro recently sat down with journalist Amna Nawaz to discuss the Republican Party's future after the midterm elections.
articles.content: Ben Shapiro, a prominent and often polarizing figure in conservative media since his teenage years, has been a dominant force in shaping right-wing discourse. Now in his early 40s, he continues to host one of America's most popular news podcasts and remains editor emeritus of The Daily Wire, a leading conservative news site. Ben Shapiro recently sat down with Amna Nawaz for an episode of "Settle In to discuss the Republican Party's future after the midterm elections. During their conversation, Amna Nawaz asked Ben Shapiro who he thinks Republicans should be considering as potential leaders. He replied that there are several candidates he would like to see run. Ben Shapiro mentioned Marco Rubio as one of his preferred choices, citing both moral and electoral reasons for his endorsement. The vice president's economic views have been a point of contention for Ben Shapiro. He has expressed concerns about the vice president's interventionist approach to economics, including tariffs and subsidies. Shapiro believes that this stance is at odds with his own views on economics, which he prefers to be more free-market oriented. This disagreement highlights one of the key challenges facing the Republican Party: finding a candidate who can appeal to both fiscal conservatives and those who favor a more active government role in the economy. The vice president's strategy of emulating Trump's coalition has been met with skepticism by Shapiro, who argues that no politician has successfully duplicated their predecessor's support base. He believes that this approach is unlikely to yield success for the vice president in 2024. Shapiro has shared his concerns with those close to the vice president on multiple occasions, but it appears that his advice has not been well-received. While he acknowledges that the vice president may be open to feedback, Shapiro reports that he rarely seeks out his counsel or advice. The vice president's prospects in key demographics are also a concern for Shapiro. For instance, winning more Hispanic votes than Trump did in 2024 seems unlikely given past trends, as well as securing blue-collar white support and female voters. These challenges underscore the difficulties of replicating Trump's coalition without significant changes to the party's message or platform. Shapiro's views on the vice president's strategy reflect a deeper concern about the Republican Party's ability to adapt to changing voter preferences and demographics. As he sees it, the party will need to find new ways to connect with voters if it hopes to remain competitive in future elections. The Republican Party is grappling with its future prospects in the wake of Donald Trump's presidency. One potential candidate who could shake things up is Marco Rubio, a former presidential nominee and current senator from Florida. In a hypothetical matchup against President Biden in 2028, Rubio's coalition might look distinctly different from Trump's. Rubio has significant disagreements with the president on several key issues, which could make it challenging for him to align himself too closely with Trump's legacy. However, according to Ben Shapiro, Rubio outperforms Trump in certain demographics, such as Hispanic voters and suburban voters. This is a notable point of divergence from the Trump campaign. In terms of game theory, Marco Rubio might be hesitant to run against President Biden in 2028. With an unpopular president on the ticket, the Republican Party faces significant headwinds. Additionally, Rubio would need to balance his own ambitions with the party's overall strategy and potential voter fatigue. Shapiro suggests that Rubio's decision not to run would be based on a rational assessment of the electoral landscape. The 2028 election is likely to favor Democrats, given the unpopularity of President Biden's predecessor. In this context, Rubio might see running as a long shot or even a liability for his own career. Rubio's potential strengths and weaknesses are closely tied to his coalition-building efforts. While he may outperform Trump in certain demographics, he also risks underperforming with blue-collar white voters. This dichotomy highlights the challenges of navigating the Republican Party's complex internal dynamics. Ultimately, Rubio's decision not to run would be a strategic one, influenced by his assessment of the party's chances and his own electoral prospects. In this sense, his hypothetical candidacy serves as a thought experiment for understanding the Republican Party's future trajectory. The Republican Party's future trajectory is being closely watched by many, particularly in light of recent polls showing President Trump's approval ratings hovering around 35%. While some predict that this momentum will carry over into a potential presidential bid, others are more skeptical. Ben Shapiro agrees with the predictions market, suggesting that it would be rare for a president to turn their approval rating around significantly. This has led him to conclude that the president's unpopularity could ultimately harm his party's chances in future elections. Shapiro pointed out that no president who left office with an unfavorable rating has seen their party win the subsequent election. In fact, several examples illustrate this point, including Barack Obama and Bill Clinton, both of whom were popular at the end of their terms but still saw their parties lose. This raises questions about the likelihood of a Republican candidate winning in 2028, particularly if they are perceived as too radical for the American people. Shapiro suggested that Democrats might inadvertently hand Republicans a victory by nominating someone like AOC, who is highly polarizing. Rubio's potential candidacy is also being weighed against the possibility of running against the vice president and potentially losing in the primaries. If he were to lose, his political career would likely be over. Shapiro noted that from a strategic perspective, Rubio might see value in waiting for 2028, rather than taking on the incumbent vice president now. This could give him a clearer path to the presidency, either as the running mate or as a potential successor. The discussion on the future of the Republican Party continues, with Ben Shapiro suggesting that Governor DeSantis could be a strong contender for the presidency. Governor DeSantis' record in Florida has been impressive, with his state being one of the few to withstand multiple blue waves. This achievement alone gives him a compelling argument to make to Republican voters. Ben Shapiro's own experience as a resident of Florida allows him to attest to the governor's success, and he believes that this could translate into a strong case for DeSantis at the national level. DeSantis' lack of baggage from being part of the administration is also seen as an advantage by Shapiro, who thinks it gives him an interesting inside track. Meanwhile, on the Democratic side, Shapiro notes that Ossoff is currently receiving a lot of attention, but he's not convinced that this momentum will last. In a recent discussion on Settle In", Ben Shapiro shared his thoughts on the Republican Party's future prospects. He noted that some candidates, despite their initial appeal, may not have enough substance to carry them through the election process. The concern for Republicans is who they will run against in the next election. When asked about this, Shapiro mentioned that he would prefer a candidate as progressive as possible, specifically Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, to give the Republican Party an easier chance of winning. However, from a purely American perspective, Shapiro expressed his desire for Democrats to nominate a relatively moderate candidate. This was not a new idea in 2020, when some Republicans debated whether it would be better to face Bernie Sanders or Joe Biden in the general election. Shapiro argued that while having Bernie Sanders as an opponent might make it easier for Trump to win, it also meant that there was a significant chance of Sanders becoming president. He preferred the idea of running against Biden, who he described as unlikable but not catastrophic. The dynamics of the Republican Party's strategy and preferences were on display in this conversation. By choosing which candidate they would prefer to run against, Republicans are making a tactical decision that could have far-reaching implications for the party's future. Ultimately, the success or failure of the Republican Party will depend on many factors, including their ability to adapt to changing circumstances and make strategic decisions about who to nominate as candidates. articles.summary: Nvidia's CEO is back in charge after a brief shake-up, but his views on succession planning are raising eyebrows among experts.
articles.content: Nvidia's Jensen Huang has been reinstated as CEO after a brief leadership shake-up, but his lack of interest in succession planning is raising eyebrows. A recent conversation between Huang and colleagues suggests that he doesn't believe in identifying potential successors, arguing that it would imply some executives are more important than others. This stance is consistent with Nvidia's unusual flat structure at the top, where decision-making power is distributed among a small group of leaders. However, experts in corporate governance warn that this approach can be short-sighted and put the company at risk if Huang were to leave suddenly. "If the CEO is hit by the proverbial bus, somebody has to be in charge," notes Umesh Ramakrishnan, cofounder and chief strategy officer at Kingsley Gate. While Huang's views on succession planning may seem unconventional, they are not without precedent. Charles Elson, founding director of the Weinberg Center for Corporate Governance at the University of Delaware, believes that boards should prioritize preparing for a future without their CEO. Nvidia's credit rating has been put on watch for possible downgrade due to concerns about its management and governance. The potential downgrade could occur within 90 days if S&P determines that governance issues persist. Executive oversight is a significant concern, with the risk of "key man" issues arising from lack of succession planning coming into focus. Governance deficiencies can be addressed by developing internal candidates for leadership roles. Nvidia's leadership structure has come under scrutiny in recent times, with some advisors suggesting it may hinder the company's ability to develop future leaders. The unusual setup, where CEO Jensen Huang has around 60 direct reports, is designed to facilitate open communication and empower employees, according to Huang himself. However, this structure may also limit opportunities for executives to gain experience running different aspects of the business. Some leadership advisors have expressed doubts about the preparedness of these executives to take on the top role, citing a lack of scale, scope, and experience as major concerns. Huang's leadership style has come under scrutiny, with some questioning his accountability in times of crisis. His willingness to take on immense responsibilities has been cited as a concern by experts who fear that Nvidia may become overly reliant on him. Kim Scott, a veteran executive and leadership trainer, warns that Nvidia would be vulnerable if it relies too heavily on Huang's singular vision. She notes that the company's future is precarious if its success hinges on one person's continued presence. articles.title: PSG's Unbeaten Streak in Champions League Ends with Late Roma Penalty
articles.summary: The result marks a significant setback for PSG, who had been riding high with a perfect record in this season's competition. Their winning run was also halted in all competitions, where they had secured 12 consecutive victories.
articles.content: Paris Saint-Germain's unbeaten streak in the Champions League has come to an end after a dramatic late penalty from Donyell Malen earned Roma a 2-2 draw at Parc des Princes on Wednesday. The result marks a significant setback for PSG, who had been riding high with a perfect record in this season's competition. Their winning run was also halted in all competitions, where they had secured 12 consecutive victories. Meanwhile, Real Madrid remains the only team with a flawless record after five league-phase matches. Roma, however, will be relieved to have salvaged a point from their visit to Paris, especially considering their collapse from a two-goal lead last time out at Manchester United. The Italian side took an early lead through Mario Hermoso's goal before being pegged back by Illia Zabarnyi's equaliser. The turning point came in the 78th minute when substitute Ousmane Dembele converted a penalty to put PSG ahead, only for Donyell Malen to seal the draw with his own spot kick. PSG's perfect Champions League record was shattered by Roma's dramatic late penalty, leaving them two points adrift of Real Madrid at the top of the standings after five matches. The Spanish side now enjoys a 100 percent record, while PSG must regroup and reassess their chances of finishing in the top eight of the 36-team table. Qualifying directly for the last 16 without a play-off round is still within reach, but it's clear that the Parisians have lost momentum. A double injury blow has weakened PSG's attack, with Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue both sidelined by ACL ruptures in recent weeks. Dembele's fitness issues only add to their woes, making it increasingly difficult for them to mount a title challenge. The absence of all five top scorers from last season's campaign further undermines PSG's prospects, with Bradley Barcola and Goncalo Ramos departed and the others either injured or unavailable. The absence of all five top scorers from last season's campaign has already been noted, but it's not just their unavailability that's causing problems for PSG. The team is also struggling to find a consistent attacking rhythm without them. Roma coach Gian Piero Gasperini made an interesting decision by leaving Malen out of his starting lineup, considering the Dutchman's impressive form this season. Malen has been in top gear, averaging over one goal per game and scoring four against Parma just last weekend. Despite their own attacking woes, Roma have still managed to find the back of the net with ease, notching 26 goals in their last seven matches before arriving in Paris. Their prolific form suggests they're a team that can adapt to any situation on the pitch. Roma took an early lead as Matias Soule's clever pass from the byline found its way to Hermoso, who was waiting to convert the chance into the back of the net. The Spanish defender's goal gave Roma a crucial advantage in the match. PSG's response was slow to come, but Ukrainian defender Zabarnyi finally got them on the board just after the half-hour mark with a well-timed header from Senny Mayulu's corner kick. The momentum had shifted decisively in favor of Roma as Dembele's penalty kick was successfully converted by PSG, but it proved to be too little, too late. Roma's hopes were reignited after a VAR check intervened and awarded them a penalty following Soule's shot being blocked by Vitinha with his raised hand in the box. Malen stepped up to take the spot-kick, capitalizing on the opportunity to score his 17th goal of an impressive campaign. The 2-2 draw ultimately sealed PSG's fate as they failed to maintain their perfect Champions League record this season, despite Dembele's efforts to salvage a win with a well-timed penalty kick.
